topics.topic: Whether an identical re-upload invalidates pending import confirmation and how to distinguish upload instances
questions: Does re-uploading byte-for-byte identical content invalidate the pending import confirmation, or does the matching digest keep it valid?
How does Registry determine that the particular upload for which confirmation was shown has been replaced when the replacement has identical bytes and therefore the same digest?

After a confirmation step is shown, must re-uploading byte-for-byte identical content invalidate that confirmation; if so, what recorded session fact lets Registry distinguish the replacement from the confirmed upload?

judgement.why: This is the same question about byte-identical re-uploads invalidating a pending confirmation, and the controlling passages are unchanged from P1.

precedent.topic: How upload identity and pending-confirmation invalidation work for successive byte-identical imports
quotes:
The uploaded file is kept in the owner session that uploaded it, in the
   process's memory only — never in the store, never on a disk — until the import is accepted, another file is uploaded in that
   session — one of the same bytes included — or the session ends (M11); then it is dropped.

Confirming a mapping after another file was uploaded in the session is
   refused: the file it named is no longer kept — also when the new file has
   the same bytes.
precedent.why: The texts expressly treat every later upload, identical bytes included, as replacing the earlier file and require the earlier confirmation to be refused; the internal mechanism used to enforce that outcome does not change observable behaviour.

topics.topic: Create-request idempotency after erasure or anonymisation removes the original request ID
questions: When an old create form is resubmitted with its original request id after the created Project was anonymised or Customer erased, must Registry preserve create idempotency or create a second record?

quotes:
A create repeated after a lost answer — with or without a caller-supplied id —
never silently makes a second project, customer or room, and never damages one.

A request id leaves its record with the values anonymisation or erasure
   removes (M01, M04); a create arriving after that with the same request id
   is a new create.
judgement.why: State 0 preserves create idempotency after a lost answer without an erasure exception, while A01 expressly treats the same request id as a new create after erasure or anonymisation removes it.

bases.rests_on:
name, phone, e-mail, language, tax id and legal name are gone (the one
    erasure covers the fiscal values, R0-06 narrowed by R0-80), and so are its
    kind, its revision, its recorded instant, the request id of its create
    and its restricted and ended marks;

unsupported_sides:
A create repeated after a lost answer — with or without a caller-supplied id —
never silently makes a second project, customer or room, and never damages one.

witness.initial: Customer C was recorded with request id K, its create answer was lost, and the owner later erased C, removing K while retaining C's identity and erased mark.
events: The owner records Customer C with request id K, but the answer is lost.
The old record-customer submission with request id K and the original facts is submitted again.
outcomes: R0-36 requires the repeat not to create a second Customer.
A01 rule 8 treats the submission as a new create and records a second Customer.
witness.observer: The owner sees either only the erased Customer or an additional newly recorded Customer.
basis:
'Create a project', 'record a customer', 'add a room' and 'publish an
   artifact pointer' each carry a request id: an opaque value the caller
   makes, unique for every create it means as new — printable text of at most
   128 characters, made from at least 16 random bytes, as a random UUID is; a
   blank one is missing (A02).

Registry keeps the request id with the record the create made, written once
   (M01, M03, M04, M05).

The owner records,
reads, corrects, restricts, ends, resumes and erases it; a service cleared
for it reads the billing data; the agent never sees it (R0-25).

A Customer is never deleted (R0-67). Recording the same person twice makes two
Customers (R0-16): Registry has no notion of "the same person".
